name: Boston
tagline: World-Class Healthcare, History, and New England Charm
description: Boston is one of America's most expensive cities but rewards residents with exceptional healthcare access, walkable neighborhoods, rich history, and a vibrant intellectual culture anchored by Harvard and MIT. The city's compact size, excellent public transit, and four distinct seasons create a European feel rare in the US. FIRE retirees face high housing and healthcare costs, but those who value culture, education, and medical access will find Boston hard to beat.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – safe in most neighborhoods, typical urban caution advised
quickFacts.climate: Continental with cold, snowy winters and warm, humid summers

housing.description: Studio in Dorchester, Revere, or Quincy (outside the core), on the Red/Orange Line

dining.description: Mostly home cooking; occasional cheap eats in Chinatown or a neighborhood spot

healthcare.description: MAGI-managed subsidized MA ConnectorCare Silver at the 2026 ConnectorCare enrollee-premium ceiling (~$235/mo in the 300–400% FPL band; $0 below 150% FPL), kept under the returned ACA 400%-FPL cliff (~$62,600 single). MA's ConnectorCare wrap prices subsidized Lean well BELOW the federal-exchange peers (PA/DC $425–470); above the cliff premium tax credits vanish and this line climbs to full price. Assumes an early retiree (45–55); older retirees budget more

transportation.description: MBTA monthly LinkPass ($90); no car needed

entertainment.description: Freedom Trail, the Esplanade, free museum hours, gym

1M.lifestyle: A studio in Dorchester, Revere, or Quincy, outside the core but on the Red or Orange Line, anchors a frugal but genuinely livable stretch of retirement. The MBTA LinkPass at $90 removes any need for a car, and the ConnectorCare-subsidized health plan keeps the stubborn US insurance line manageable as long as taxable income stays under the returned ACA cliff. Meals are mostly cooked at home, with the odd cheap plate in Chinatown or a neighborhood spot. Winter heating is a real line in the utilities, but the Freedom Trail, the Charles River Esplanade, and free museum hours make the entertainment budget stretch. Housing takes the majority of the budget — Boston's floor simply does not fall further.

housing.description: Comfortable 1BR in Quincy, Somerville, or Jamaica Plain

dining.description: Out several times a week across the mid-range scene

healthcare.description: Unsubsidized MA Silver (above the cliff at a FIRE income); MA's compressed 2:1 age band keeps escalation moderate

2M.lifestyle: A comfortable one-bedroom in Quincy, Somerville, or Jamaica Plain buys a real neighborhood with an easy commute into the core. Dining out lands several times a week across the city's mid-range scene, a proper unsubsidized Silver plan covers healthcare, and the LinkPass with an occasional rideshare or Zipcar keeps a car unnecessary. Memberships, a gym, and regular outings fit the budget, along with weekend trips to the North Shore or the Cape. It is Boston lived comfortably rather than lavishly, with the walkability and transit doing a lot of the work.

housing.description: 1BR or small 2BR in Back Bay, Beacon Hill, or Cambridge

dining.description: Regular dining out in the North End and South End

healthcare.description: Unsubsidized MA Silver/Gold (above the cliff), with Mass General / Brigham networks

transportation.description: LinkPass plus regular rideshare and occasional Zipcar

entertainment.description: Theater, a museum membership, Red Sox games

3M.lifestyle: A one-bedroom or small two-bedroom in Back Bay, Beacon Hill, or Cambridge puts daily life in the heart of one of America's most walkable cities. Dining out is a regular habit across the North End and South End, healthcare is a proper unsubsidized plan with access to Mass General and Brigham networks, and the T plus the occasional Zipcar or rideshare covers getting around without owning a car. Theater, a museum membership, and Red Sox games fit comfortably, as do weekend drives to Cape Cod or the Berkshires. At $6,000 a month, Boston feels genuinely comfortable, with the country's best concentration of hospitals a short ride away.

housing.description: Luxury high-rise unit in the Seaport or a refined Back Bay address

dining.description: Near-daily fine dining at the city's best tables

healthcare.description: Top-tier plan plus a concierge / direct-primary-care retainer (Mass General / Dana-Farber)

transportation.description: Premium rideshare and car service, Zipcar/rental for weekends

luxuryExtras.description: Concierge services, wellness, club dues, travel fund

5M.lifestyle: A luxury high-rise unit in the Seaport or a refined Back Bay address, with a housekeeper on a weekly rhythm, marks a clearly upper-affluent Boston life. Fine dining is a near-daily option, healthcare adds a concierge or direct-primary-care retainer on top of a top-tier plan, and transport leans on premium rideshare and car service with a Zipcar or rental for weekends. Theater subscriptions, premium memberships, and summer stays on Nantucket or Martha's Vineyard are comfortable, as is business-class travel. This is living very well in an expensive city, renting the best neighborhoods rather than buying them.

housing.description: Historic Beacon Hill townhouse floor or waterfront Seaport/Marblehead residence

dining.description: Daily fine dining at the city's best rooms

healthcare.description: Top-tier plan plus premium concierge at Mass General / Dana-Farber

entertainment.description: Fenway box seats, MFA/BSO patronage, clubs

domesticHelp.description: Housekeeping a couple of days a week plus part-time personal-assistant hours

luxuryExtras.description: First-class travel, art/philanthropy, Cape Cod or Nantucket stays

10M.lifestyle: A historic Beacon Hill townhouse floor or a waterfront Seaport residence, with housekeeping a couple of days a week and part-time assistant support, defines life at the top of Boston. Dining is daily at the city's best tables, healthcare pairs a top-tier plan with concierge access at Mass General or Dana-Farber, and a private car service handles the New England seasons. Box seats at Fenway, patron-level support of the MFA and the BSO, and summers on Cape Cod or Nantucket are all within reach. First-class travel and an art or philanthropy budget round out a life where the bill is never the question. Boston's medical depth makes this arguably the best place in the country to age with means.
